subject: Insurance
title: Chinese River Merchants
description: A quick, practical guide to Chinese River Merchants.

hook.text: Ancient Chinese merchants split cargo across many boats. If one sank, no single trader lost everything.

buildup.text: Yangtze River rapids destroyed boats regularly. Merchants needed a system to survive unpredictable losses.

discovery.text: By spreading risk across the group, each merchant turned a catastrophic loss into a small, manageable one.

twist.text: This wasn't charity. It was calculated self-interest. Every merchant knew they'd need the same help someday.

climax.text: Risk pooling—the core of all insurance—was invented by traders who simply couldn't afford to lose alone.

punchline.text: Split the cargo, share the risk. Chinese merchants invented pooling.

quiz.question: How did Chinese merchants manage shipping risk?
